questions.q: What is the real shape of a strong answer to a scenario-based DBA interview question, per this lesson?
options: Ask the interviewer to skip to the next question
Immediately propose the most expensive or complex solution available
Clarify the actual constraint, name the relevant tool or concept, explain the trade-off, then state what you'd verify afterward
Recite the textbook definition of the relevant feature as quickly as possible
questions.explain: This is the same shape Chapter 15's real-world project made you practice on one continuous scenario — reciting a definition without it reads as memorized, not understood.

questions.q: For "a query was fast yesterday, slow today, with no code changes," what should a strong answer name first?
options: Azure Policy compliance settings
Query Store, since this is exactly the regression-detection scenario it was built for
Restarting the database engine
Immediately rebuilding every index on the server
questions.explain: Query Store (Lessons 48-49) is purpose-built to catch exactly this kind of plan regression.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize being able to explain RPO and RTO in plain, non-technical language?
options: Plain-language explanations are less accurate than technical ones
Being able to drop the jargon on request, in two plain sentences, is itself a real interview signal of genuine understanding
Non-technical stakeholders never need to understand RPO or RTO
RPO and RTO have no real meaning outside of technical documentation
questions.explain: Translating a technical concept for a non-technical audience on demand demonstrates real understanding, not memorization.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does finishing this course (Lesson 95) actually complete in the Azure Database Administrator career path?
options: Only this single course, with no relationship to the broader career path
The entire career path, including its Advanced stage, with nothing left to build
The Job-Ready stage — alongside T-SQL Development, Azure Fundamentals, and Data Factory — but NOT the Advanced stage, which still needs PowerShell Fundamentals
The Advanced stage specifically, while the Job-Ready stage remains incomplete
questions.explain: This course is precise about scope — Job-Ready stage complete, Advanced stage still has PowerShell Fundamentals ahead of it.

questions.q: For "how would you prove to an auditor that a table's history wasn't tampered with," which feature does this lesson say specifically answers that?
options: Azure CLI command history
SQL Server Agent job history
Dynamic Data Masking, since it hides sensitive values
Ledger — because Change Tracking or plain SQL Auditing alone wouldn't satisfy that specific tamper-evidence requirement
questions.explain: This ties directly back to Lesson 37's distinction between logging (auditing), sync tracking (Change Tracking), and cryptographic tamper-evidence (Ledger).
